attributes.nuance_translation: An expression that focuses on the journey between (A) and (B).

attributes.body:
へ行（い）く is a common construction used when describing a place that someone/something is 'heading'. The particles に and へ are mostly interchangeable, but there is a slight difference in meaning. に has the nuance of 'going to', while へ has the nuance of 'heading to'.

In these examples, while they may seem the same at first glance, へ focuses much more on the journey, while に puts more emphasis on the destination. This is true for other uses of に and へ as well. に will always put more focus on the destination of an action, where へ will put more emphasis on the distance traveled/between the origin and destination.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.body: The へ in both patterns is the same directional particle. While it's commonly used with いく to indicate going somewhere or moving in a direction (e.g., 学校へいく, 西へいく), it can also be used with other verbs (e.g., 家へ帰る, 公園へ歩く) or in certain phrases (e.g., 東京へようこそ！). In all cases, へ expresses directionality or movement toward a location.

second_relatable.title: へいく
second_relatable.meaning: To go to, To head toward

attributes.body: The verb いく expresses movement in a direction, literally or figuratively. へいく is used after nouns to indicate moving toward a place (e.g., 学校へいく = 'go to school'). When used as ていく (Verb + て + いく), it implies a continuing action or change moving forward. Note that いく is written in kanji as 行く when used alone, but typically in hiragana in the ていく form.

first_relatable.title: へいく
first_relatable.meaning: To go to, To head toward

second_relatable.title: ていく
second_relatable.meaning: To ~ and go, To go on, To start

attributes.body: くる and いく are both movement verbs often used with directional particles to express moving toward a particular location. The difference lies in the perspective of the speaker and directionality: くる typically expresses movement toward the speaker's location, while いく expresses movement away from the speaker's location.

second_relatable.title: へいく
second_relatable.meaning: To go to, To head toward

attributes.body: へいく is used with nouns, typically physical locations or directions, to express 'going' or 'heading' somewhere (e.g., 学校へいく, 西へいく). へ can be replaced with に, which is more colloquial and emphasizes the final destination. にいく can also combine with verb stems to express going to perform an action (e.g., 食べにいく = 'go to eat'). The two patterns can be combined as well (e.g., 店へ食べにいく = 'go to the store to eat').

first_relatable.title: へいく
first_relatable.meaning: To go to, To head toward

second_relatable.title: Verb + にいく
second_relatable.meaning: To go ~, To go in order to ~

attributes.body: Both いらっしゃる and いく express movement away from the speaker, similar to the English 'go.' The key difference is politeness: いく is a neutral verb used in everyday contexts, while いらっしゃる is a polite, honorific verb used to show respect for someone's movement. Note that いらっしゃる also serves as the honorific form of いる, くる, and いく.
